quote: I have solar panels on on my house. I'm with Vivint Solar already.
stewart_read: Existing-system disclosure at the very top of the call — the orphaned_flow steps (own/lease, company, size, working) should trigger immediately rather than pivoting to a battery/panels sales question.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally warming up before the DQ question to see if there's an add-on opportunity; but no add-on materialized and the DQ gate is what mattered.
coaching_implication: Ask ownership status (lease vs loan/cash) within the first exchange after any existing-solar disclosure — it is the fastest DQ gate available.

quote: The panels we use, I believe that they are 440 watts.
stewart_read: Rep answers a technical spec question directly instead of using the escape hatch to redirect to a specialist.
coaching_implication: Use the universal escape hatch language for spec questions: that's exactly what the specialist walks through.

quote: Talk about the data centers and whatnot.
stewart_read: This line is confusing and untethered — it reads as a rushed or garbled attempt to explain rising utility costs but lands as noise rather than a hook.
alternative_hypothesis: Possible transcription artifact / diarization garble rather than a true rep failure — the line is incoherent enough that it may not fully represent what was said.
coaching_implication: If this was an attempt to explain rate hikes, it needs to be a clean, simple line tied to the customer's own bill, not a vague aside.

quote: My electric bill used to be, like, $15.20
stewart_read: This bill figure is confusing (likely a misheard/garbled $150-something) and directly contradicts the customer's earlier $200-and-something claim; the rep never reconciles or clarifies it, leaving the anchor unusable.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be a diarization/transcription error on the number itself rather than a rep miss, but the rep still had an opening to ask 'so is it closer to $200 now?' and didn't.
coaching_implication: When a stated bill number contradicts an earlier one, clarify on the spot rather than letting it pass — an ambiguous anchor is worse than no anchor.

quote: I I I'll think about it and perhaps call back.
stewart_read: This is a soft timing/interest objection; rep does not attempt a flip or curiosity-creation response and instead moves straight into address verification.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer is about to be disqualified on lease status anyway, continuing to the DQ-determining questions was the higher-value move rather than fighting a deferral on a likely-dead lead.
coaching_implication: On a live lease-disclosed lead, resolving the DQ gate quickly (as the rep did next) is defensible; but if the lead were qualifiable, this deferral needed a flip attempt.

quote: Vivint, do you own it or are you leasing it?
stewart_read: This is the correct DQ-determining question, but it arrives last, after two minutes of tangential bill/pricing talk that had no bearing on qualification.
coaching_implication: Move this question to immediately follow any existing-solar disclosure to avoid wasted call time on unqualifiable leads.
